title: Changing velocity
target: Calculate acceleration and distinguish speeding up, slowing down, and turning.
criteria: Calculate acceleration from velocity change and time.
Compare acceleration direction with velocity direction.
Explain why turning at steady speed is acceleration.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Velocity changes from +2 to +14 m/s in 4 s. What is average acceleration?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: With east positive, velocity changes from −9 to −3 m/s in 2 s. What is average acceleration?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A cart moves left while its acceleration points right. What happens to its speed initially?
options: It remains constant under nonzero acceleration.
cpa.guide: Opposing velocity and acceleration reduce speed initially.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An object has negative velocity and negative acceleration along one axis. What is happening to its speed?
options: It is constant because both signs match.
cpa.guide: Same-direction velocity and acceleration increase speed magnitude.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A skater turns while keeping speed constant. Which statement is correct?
options: Acceleration is zero because speed is constant.
Velocity changes direction, so acceleration is nonzero.
cpa.guide: Acceleration tracks change in the velocity vector.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which motion necessarily has zero average acceleration over the interval?
options: Initial and final velocity vectors are identical.
The path is curved at constant speed between different tangent directions.
The object ends at its starting position with unspecified velocities.
Initial and final speeds are equal but directions differ.
cpa.guide: Average acceleration depends on vector Δv, not path length or displacement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
